input.source_text: class A { property tag: Symbol = arm() public fun initialize() -> Object { nil } public fun arm() -> Symbol { let committed = A.open() { |t| t.define_method(:m) { :new } }; :armed } public fun m() -> Symbol { :old } } module Q { public fun run() -> Object { let a = A.new(); [a.tag, a.m()] } } Q.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C056 snapshots A's active revision at construction START for allocation, layout, stored property initialization and the INITIAL `initialize` dispatch, and continues with it when a new revision commits before construction completes. The mechanism was already implemented - `runtime.construct` clones the active revision and dispatches `initialize` through that snapshot - and the rows were held because their schedule is prose with no way to land a commit mid-construction. A stored-property initializer supplies one: it runs BEFORE the initial dispatch, so committing a replacement from inside it is a genuine mid-construction commit. The ORIGINAL initialize then runs, while the same replacement committed BEFORE construction does take effect, which is what makes this evidence of the snapshot rather than of the replacement never working.
